Who is broadcasting Super Bowl 2026? A guide to the TV channel, announcers & more on Super Bowl 60 rights originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The 2026 Super Bowl is just a few weeks away, and although the matchup isn't set, we do know which television network will broadcast the big game.

Advertisement

Advertisement

Broadcasting the Super Bowl is seen as the pinnacle for television networks, which is why several different ones bid to earn the rights for the big game year after year. Last year, a whopping 127.7 million viewers watched the Philadelphia Eagles' 40-22 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs, making it the most-watched Super Bowl ever.

2026's Super Bowl will mark a busy month of February for the host network that gets the honor.

Here are the details about the Super Bowl 60 broadcast and how you can watch it.

MORE: Revisiting the highest-scoring Super Bowl ever.

## Who is broadcasting the Super Bowl in 2026?

NBC is broadcasting Super Bowl 60 between the future AFC and NFC champions on Feb. 8, 2026.

Advertisement

Advertisement

The network is part of a rotation between four other networks in Fox, CBS and ABC for the game. As part of the NBC's current deal, the network gets to broadcast the Super Bowl during the same year its hosting the Winter Olympics, also taking place in Feb. 2026.

The game will also be streamed on NBC's app, Peacock.

The Super Bowl airing on NBC marks the first time the network has hosted the game since 2022, the same year the network held the last Winter Olympics.

Normally Super Bowl 59 would be NBC's spot in the rotation; however, the network flipped with Fox so it could cover Super Bowl 60, which coincides ahead of the 2026 Summer Olympics on NBC.

## How much does it cost to broadcast the Super Bowl?

Instead of the NFL selling the rights to the game individually, the cost to cover the Super Bowl is included in what networks pay to broadcast NFL games in general.

CBS, Fox and NBC are all paying upwards of $2 billion to host games in the current television deals, which started in 2023 and go through 2033. ABC, which includes ESPN, paid $2.7 billion.

These numbers are more than double what each side paid under the previous deal, which was in place before the new contracts were agreed upon in 2021.MORE: How the Super Bowl's name traces back to to a 1960s toy

## Super Bowl announcers: Mike Tirico and Cris Collinsworth

NFL fans will be pretty used to the Super Bowl announcing crew. It is composed of NBC's "Sunday Night Football" crew in play-by-play announcer Mike Tirico and Cris Collinsworth. This will mark Collinsworth's fourth Super Bowl, previously doing so alongside Al Michaels in years past.

It will also mark the first time that Tirico calls a Super Bowl for the first time in his career. He will also be leading NBC's coverage from Italy for the Winter Olympics, so it will be a busy month for the longtime broadcaster. MORE: Super Bowl coin toss history

## Super Bowl sideline reporters: Melissa Stark, Kaylee Hartung

The sideline reporters Melissa Stark and Kaylee Hartung will also be broadcasting a Super Bowl for the very first time in their careers. Hartung, who is the lead sideline reporter for Amazon Prime's NFL Thursday night games, was announced for the job just on Jan. 14. It will mark the first Super Bowl for Stark as well, who has been NBC's SNF sideline reporter since 2022.

The Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots are just days away from their fateful date with NFL destiny, dialing in those oh-so-crucial final football preparations as the NFC and AFC get set to collide on NBC and Peacock in Super Bowl LX.

## How to Watch

Watch Sunday Night Football on NBC and streaming on Peacock.

Super Bowl Sunday on February 8 marks the pinnacle of NBC Sports’ football calendar, crowning a full season of stellar weekly NFL matchups on NBC’s Sunday Night Football. Together with the studio squad on Football Night in America, the SNF broadcast team has been there to capture each week’s hard-hitting, high-flying NFL action in all its larger-than-life glory — and now they’re locked in to do it again for the biggest game of the year, complete with a super-sized coverage crew to bring viewers every unforgettable moment from Super Bowl LX.

RELATED: How Mike Tirico Will "Lock In" for Super Bowl, Olympics & NBA in Legendary February (EXCLUSIVE)

## Everything to know about NBC Sports’ broadcast team for Super Bowl LX

Cris Collinsworth looks on from the sideline before a game between the Kansas City Chiefs and Pittsburgh SteelersMike Tirico appears on TODAY on Thursday, May 11, 2023; Melissa Stark attends the Prime-Time Champions: An Evening with NBC Sunday Night Football Photo: Getty Images

Fun fact: Super Bowl LX serves up a rare Super Bowl rematch, pitting the Seahawks against the Patriots once again after their first Super Bowl meeting in 2015 (which the Patriots won). Want another fun fact? Super Bowl LX will mark the very first Super Bowl game call for ace SNF play-by-play veteran Mike Tirico, who’ll be joined by an entire ensemble of NBC Sports broadcasters to cover all the action at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, California from every conceivable angle.

Here’s a closer look at the complete NBC Sports broadcast team who’ll be on the call, in the studio, and absolutely all over the stadium (including the sidelines!) for Super Bowl LX:

### On the call: Play-by-play, commentary, and analysis

In-game coverage for Super Bowl LX features a tight-knit unit of welcome and familiar names. After all, it’s the same coverage team fans look forward to joining every week for Sunday Night Football.

NBC Sports’ Emmy Award-winning Super Bowl LX broadcast team will be led by Mike Tirico, the lead play-by-play voice of Sunday Night Football. Tirico will be calling his first-ever Super Bowl on February 8, just ahead of his epic two-week stint in northern Italy to serve as the nightly prime time host for NBC’s coverage of the Milan Cortina Winter Olympics.

Joining Tirico in the Super Bowl broadcast booth will be 17-time Emmy Award-winning analyst Cris Collinsworth, who’ll be covering his sixth Super Bowl. Melissa Stark (second Super Bowl) and Kaylee Hartung (first Super Bowl assignment) will serve as the game’s sideline reporters, while three-time Super Bowl referee Terry McAulay will provide expert rules analysis for his second Super Bowl with NBC Sports.

RELATED: Everything to Know About Super Bowl LX: Time, Location, Halftime Show & More

Sunday Night Football on NBC & Peacock

The NFL returns to NBC and Peacock this fall with some of the biggest games of the season thanks to Sunday Night Football for the 2026-2027 season.

Football fans got a chance to see the Seattle Seahawks take down the New England Patriots at the end of last season in Super Bowl LX, exclusively on NBC and Peacock. Keep an eye on NBC Insider for the latest info on the schedule and how to watch the biggest NFL games on NBC and Peacock all season-long.

### In the studio: Super Bowl LX pregame coverage

Maria Taylor attends A Celebration of Olympic Basketball at Team USA House, Palais Brongniart on August 5, 2024 in Paris, France.

Photo: Victor Boyko/Getty Images

NBC Sports is assembling the complete Football Night in America team for a jumbo five-hour Super Bowl LX pregame show. FNIA host Maria Taylor will serve as the lead studio host for her first-ever Super Bowl pregame — all before scooting down to the field to host the postgame presentation of the winning team’s Vince Lombardi Trophy.

Right beside Taylor in the pregame studio will be Jac Collinsworth (second Super Bowl assignment) and Noah Eagle (in his Super Bowl debut for NBC Sports), each serving as pregame co-hosts alongside Super Bowl champion analysts Tony Dungy, Jason Garrett, Rodney Harrison, and Devin McCourty.

Dungy won his first Super Bowl as a player with the Pittsburgh Steelers (Super Bowl XIII), and then did it again as the head coach of the Indianapolis Colts (Super Bowl XLI). Garrett won three Super Bowls with the Dallas Cowboys (Super Bowls XXVII, XXVIII, and XXX). Harrison won two Super Bowls with the New England Patriots (Super Bowls XXXVIII and XXXIX); while McCourty won three Super Bowls with the Patriots (Super Bowls XLIX, LI, and LIII).

RELATED: Super Bowl LX: Why Does the Super Bowl Use Roman Numerals?

### More Super Bowl LX coverage: In the studio and on location

Also live to deliver more views from Super Bowl Sunday will be an elite team of NFL and NBC Sports broadcasting talent. Former NFL quarterback Chris Simms will return as a Super Bowl analyst alongside his Football Night in America teammate and NBC Sports insider Mike Florio.

For Florio, this year’s title game will mark his 17th Super Bowl, where he’ll deliver on-location reporting on all the news surrounding Super Bowl LX. Steve Kornacki, NBC News’ celebrated political correspondent, will also return to run the numbers for the Super Bowl pregame show, while FNIA fantasy football and sports betting expert Matthew Berry will make his Super Bowl debut with NBC Sports. Finally, Access Hollywood’s Kit Hoover will be live and on location, conducting interviews from the NFL Tailgate at Levi’s Stadium.

Need a postgame nightcap to wrap your head around everything the NFL just threw at you? Florio and Simms will be hosting a special edition of Florio’s PFT (Pro Football Talk) Live webcast, coming straight from the field after Super Bowl LX at 11 p.m. ET.

All of NBC Sports’ Super Bowl Sunday coverage will air live on Sunday, February 8 as the Seahawks and Patriots face off in Super Bowl LX at Levi’s Stadium. Pregame coverage begins at 1 p.m. ET, followed by the Super Bowl LX Opening Ceremony at 6 p.m. ET and kickoff at 6:30 p.m. ET. From start to finish, you can catch all the day’s Super Bowl LX action live on NBC, and in simulcast streaming on Peacock.

# SUPER BOWL LX IS SECOND MOST-WATCHED ALL-TIME WITH 125.6 MILLION VIEWERS, PEAKING AT ALL-TIME U.S. RECORD 137.8 MILLION VIEWERS ACROSS NBC, PEACOCK, AND TELEMUNDO

Published February 10, 2026 06:47 PM

Seahawks-Patriots is Most-Watched Show in History of NBC, Which Celebrates 100 Years in 2026

Apple Music Super Bowl LX Halftime Show Featuring Global Superstar Bad Bunny Generates Over 4 Billion Social Views in First 24 Hours – up 137% - the Most-Consumed Halftime Show of All-Time on NFL Social Platforms

Telemundo Delivers Largest Spanish-Language NFL Game Audience Ever; Peacock Achieves Best Day Ever on Sunday

Sunday’s Milan Cortina Olympics Presentation Averages 42 Million Viewers, Marking Largest Winter Games Audience since Day 2 of 2014 Sochi Olympics

STAMFORD, Conn. – Updated February 19, 2026 – NBC Sports’ presentation of Super Bowl LX set an all-time media record as 137.8 million viewers watched in the second quarter as the Seattle Seahawks led 6-0 over the New England Patriots – marking the highest peak viewership in U.S. TV history.

The Seahawks’ 29-13 victory over the Patriots averaged 125.6 million viewers on NBC, Peacock, Telemundo, NBC Sports Digital, and NFL+, based on official live + same day Nielsen Big Data + Panel, ranking as the second-most watched show in U.S. history (behind Super Bowl LIX on FOX in Feb. 2025).

Super Bowl LX is the most-watched show in the history of NBCUniversal, which celebrates 100 years of NBC in 2026.

“The Super Bowl and the NFL once again delivered a blockbuster audience across the NBC broadcast network, Peacock, and Telemundo, and provided an unprecedented lead-in to our Primetime in Milan coverage,” said Rick Cordella, President, NBC Sports. “The Super Bowl and the Olympics are the two most powerful events in the world, and we salute our talented production, tech, and announce teams who delivered best-in-class presentations for our viewers, stations, and partners.”

Super Bowl LX capped NBC Sports’ milestone 20th season of Sunday Night Football, which delivered a record audience (23.5 million viewers) and is pacing as primetime’s No. 1 show for an unprecedented 15th consecutive season.

Telemundo Delivers Most Watched Super Bowl in U.S. Spanish-Language History

Telemundo averaged 3.3 million viewers, marking the most-watched Super Bowl in U.S. Spanish-language history. Telemundo’s audience peaked during the halftime show, with an average of 4.8 million viewers – the most-watched Super Bowl halftime in Spanish-language history.

Apple Music Super Bowl LX Halftime Show Breaks All-Time NFL Records on Social Media

Total social consumption (inclusive of fans, owned platforms, broadcast partners, influencers, etc.) of the Apple Music Super Bowl LX Halftime Show starring Bad Bunny set a record of four billion views after the first 24 hours, up 137% YoY (Source: Ripple Analytics).

Over 55% of all NFL social views of the Apple Music Super Bowl LX Halftime Show came from international markets.

The top three most-viewed NFL social posts in history are now Apple Music Super Bowl LX Halftime Show clips. In total, these clips have been viewed for over 115 years on social media platforms.

- “ Only Thing More Powerful Than Hate is Love” - @NFL on Instagram - 179M views, most viewed clip on NFL Social ever – 54% of views coming from outside the United States
- Bad Bunny Listing Countries before Spiking Football- @NFL on Instagram -168M views, second most watched clip on NFL social ever - 68% of views coming from outside the United States
- Bad Bunny Listing Countries Before Spiking Football– @NFL on TikTok – 100 million views; people have spent a combined 53+ years watching this clip already; 60% of the viewership is female, 62% comes from outside the United States; 91% of viewers under 35; 36% under 25

The Apple Music Super Bowl LX Halftime Show averaged 128.2 million viewers from 8:15-8:30 p.m. ET in the United States. Full global viewership for the Apple Music Super Bowl LX Halftime Show will be available early next week.

Bad Bunny on Apple Music

Immediately following the Apple Music Super Bowl LX Halftime Show, Bad Bunny listens on Apple Music were up 7x. “DtMF,” “BAILE INoLVIDABLE,” and “Tití Me Preguntó” were the most streamed songs immediately after the show. Other Apple Music notables from the Halftime Show include:

- In the hours following his performance, Bad Bunny’s Apple Music Super Bowl LX Halftime Show Set List playlist became the most-played Set List on Apple Music.
- The day after Super Bowl LX, Bad Bunny’s DeBÍ TiRAR MáS FOToS landed on the album charts in 155 countries, reaching the Top 10 in 128 countries and claiming the #1 spot in 46 countries, including Mexico, Colombia, Chile, Brazil, Germany, France and Spain.

Following his appearance in the Apple Music Super Bowl LX Halftime Show, Bad Bunny occupied nearly a quarter of the Daily Top 100 Global chart, with 24 songs in the Top 100, 9 songs in the Top 25, and 6 songs in the Top 10, including “DtMF,” which was the #1 song.

- 6 of the 24 songs re-entered the Daily Top 100 Global chart for the first time since at least February 2025, and his single with Cardi B, “I Like It,” re-entered the chart for the first time since January 2020.

Sunday’s Milan Cortina Winter Olympics Presentation Averaged 42 Million Viewers

Following the Vince Lombardi Trophy presentation on the field at Levi’s Stadium, Super Bowl LX play-by-play voice Mike Tirico hosted Primetime in Milan, which featured Lindsey Vonn’s downhill run, and gold-medal winning performances by Breezy Johnson in the downhill and Team USA in the team figure skating event at the Milan Cortina Winter Olympics.

Sunday’s Primetime in Milan and Milan Prime presentation averaged 42 million viewers, marking NBCUniversal’s largest Winter Games audience since Day 2 of the 2014 Sochi Olympics (a span of 53 event days) and an increase of 73% over the corresponding 2022 Beijing Olympics show (24.3 million) which followed Super Bowl LVI.

Peacock Achieves Best Day Ever

Sunday was Peacock’s best day ever in terms of both reach and hours streamed, and featured the post-Super Bowl debut of “The Burbs,” which was the highest Day 1 Peacock original debut ever.

More detailed viewership metrics will be available from Nielsen later this week.

Legendary February Ad Scale and Impact

NBC/Peacock drove the lifts in breakthrough, at scale, for custom marketing integrations in Super Bowl LX. Compared to competitive NFL broadcasts (Regular Season + Playoffs), NBCU delivered sponsors:

- +33% lift in brand recall
- +31% lift in brand opinion

# Who Is Broadcasting the Super Bowl This Year?

Recognize that voice? Dive into our guide to discover who's calling Super Bowl LX on Sunday, February 8, at 6:30 p.m. ET.

Under the current Super Bowl broadcast deal, the NFL’s championship game rotates each year between ABC, CBS, FOX, and NBC. But 2026 is a bit different.

This year, NBC Sports takes center stage for what it calls “Super Gold Sunday.” It’s a historic broadcasting event where Super Bowl LX and the Milan Cortina Winter Olympics converge on a single day, spanning the entire NBCUniversal portfolio. That means the Seahawks–Patriots matchup will air on NBC and Peacock, while Telemundo and UNIVERSO team up for the exclusive Spanish-language broadcast.

Of course, the Super Bowl coverage will feature a star-studded lineup of commentators, analysts, hosts, and insiders. Keep reading as I dive into which TV personalities will be on hand at Super Bowl LX.

## Super Bowl LX on NBC

NBC is the official English-language broadcaster for Super Bowl LX, delivering the action to millions of viewers nationwide. You can expect the network to go all-in on this year’s matchup between the Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots.

Here’s a closer look at who’ll be behind the mic and what to watch for on Super Bowl Sunday.

NBC Super Bowl Broadcast Team

Play-by-play: Mike Tirico Analyst: Cris Collinsworth Sideline reporters: Melissa Stark, Kaylee Hartung Rules expert: Terry McAulay

### Who’s announcing the Super Bowl on NBC?

Play-by-play announcer Mike Tirico and analyst Cris Collinsworth will lead NBC’s Super Bowl LX coverage. While Collinsworth is a veteran of the big game (this is his sixth time in the booth), this marks Tirico’s first time calling a Super Bowl.

They’ll be joined by sideline reporters Melissa Stark and Kaylee Hartung, with three-time Super Bowl referee Terry McAulay serving as the rules analyst.

### Is there a preshow before the Super Bowl?

Leading into the main broadcast, NBC will air a massive five-hour pregame show starting at 1:00 p.m. ET.

Football Night in America host Maria Taylor will anchor the coverage alongside a deep roster of analysts, including Hall of Famer Tony Dungy, Jason Garrett, Rodney Harrison, and Devin McCourty.

Additional pregame coverage will feature co-hosts Jac Collinsworth and Noah Eagle. You can also expect to see contributions from the following industry experts.

- Chris Simms (analyst)
- Mike Florio (NBC Sports insider)
- Steve Kornacki (NBC News national political correspondent)
- Matthew Berry (Fantasy sports and betting analyst)
- Kit Hoover (Access Hollywood host, reporting from the tailgate)

### Who presents the Super Bowl trophy?

Once the Super Bowl ends, NBC host Maria Taylor will present the Vince Lombardi Trophy to the winning team and its owners.

But don’t turn off the TV just yet. Immediately following the postgame ceremonies (approximately 10:45 p.m. ET), NBC will pivot to Winter Olympics coverage with Primetime in Milan, featuring updates from the Milano Cortina 2026 games.

Lights, camera, action! Super Bowl LX will be captured from every angle, with NBC Sports using more than 80 cameras for the 4K HDR broadcast.

## Super Bowl LX on Telemundo

Telemundo and UNIVERSO will also air Super Bowl LX en Español, marking the flagship Spanish-language network’s third time covering the Big Game. Coverage will begin with the Camino al Super Bowl pregame show at 1:00 p.m. ET. Featuring top network personalities, the show will offer analysis, debates, and cultural stories from Santa Clara.

Following the game, Homenaje al Campeón airs at 10:15 p.m. ET, with postgame analysis and the Lombardi Trophy presentation. Then, 30 minutes later, Super Bowl LX: Extra will wrap up the night at Levi’s Stadium.

Telemundo Super Bowl Broadcast Team

Play-by-play: Miguel Gurwitz Analyst: Rolando Cantú Reporter: Adriana Monsalve

### Who’s announcing the Super Bowl on Telemundo?

Emmy Award-winning play-by-play announcer Miguel Gurwitz and former Arizona Cardinals offensive lineman Rolando Cantú will lead the Spanish-language call. Sports reporter Adriana Monsalve will join them in the booth.

## Super Bowl broadcast FAQ

### Who's singing the 2026 Super Bowl national anthem?

Charlie Puth will be performing "The Star Spangled Banner" during the 2026 Super Bowl pregame show. Other pregame performances include Brandi Carlile taking on "America the Beautiful" and Coco Jones singing "Lift Every Voice and Sing."

### What time is the Super Bowl flyover?

The Super Bowl flyover typically occurs during the national anthem, just before kickoff at around 6:20 p.m. ET. This year, the U.S. Air Force and the U.S. Navy will fly B-1 Lancers, F-15C Eagles, F/A-18E Super Hornets, and F-35C Lightning IIs over Levi's Stadium, though the exact flyover time may vary on game day.

### Who’s playing the Super Bowl halftime show?

Global superstar Bad Bunny headlines the Super Bowl LX Halftime Show. In a historic first, the performance will feature a multilingual signing program incorporating Puerto Rican Sign Language with deaf performer Celimar Rivera Cosme.

### Is the Super Bowl broadcast on radio?

Yes, the main Super Bowl radio broadcast will air on Westwood One affiliate stations. You can also stream the broadcast live through the NFL app with an NFL+ subscription.

# ‘This is America’s game’: What fans can expect from CT-based NBC Sports’ Super Bowl LX coverage

By Paul Schott, Staff WriterFeb 5, 2026

A file photo of Mike Tirico, the play-by-play announcer of NBC Sports' Sunday Night Football. Tirico will serve in the same role during NBC Sports' broadcast of Super Bowl LX on Feb. 8, 2026.

Jeff Haynes / Associated Press

The New England Patriots and the Seattle Seahawks will meet Sunday in Super Bowl LX at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, California. But the game will still have strong Connecticut connections.

NBC Sports will deploy a game day crew of about 700 people in Santa Clara, as well as about 40 team members at its headquarters in Stamford, to deliver its coverage of the premier event in American professional sports. The group will be led by Rob Hyland, the coordinating producer of NBC Sports’ “ Sunday Night Football,” the most-watched, prime-time television show in the U.S.

“I remember my first Super Bowl, sitting down in the living room of my parents’ house. It was Super Bowl XX, the Patriots and Bears. With its coverage of Super Bowl LX, NBC Sports will aim to surpass the massive audiences garnered by previous Super Bowls. In last year’s title game, the Philadelphia Eagles’ 40-22 defeat of the Kansas City Chiefs was watched by an average of nearly 128 million viewers. “The end result is a matchup of two of the best teams, the Seahawks and Patriots, for the championship. Yes, people would tune in regardless of which network owns the broadcast rights. # Nielsen revises Super Bowl LX final rating to 125.6 million viewers

Published: Feb 20, 2026 at 10:31 AM

- Copied!

NEW YORK -- The average viewer numbers for the Super Bowl increased to 125.6 million after Nielsen released its final viewer figures on Thursday for the Feb. 8 game.

It was a 700,000 increase from the original number of 124.9 million, which was released on Feb. 10.

Nielsen attributed the update to a Big Data provider not properly collecting data from its devices on Feb. 8. Nielsen began using its Big Data + Panel methodology for all events last September with the start of the current television season.

results.title: Super Bowl LX, Bad Bunny's halftime fall shy of ratings records - ESPN
results.author: Nate Taylor
results.text:
Super Bowl LX, Bad Bunny's halftime fall shy of ratings records - ESPN

Skip to main content Skip to navigation

<

>

play

Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald joins Scott Van Pelt to speak about Seattle's Super Bowl win vs. the Patriots. (0:40)

Sunday night's Super Bowl and Bad Bunny fell short of setting records for most-watched U.S. broadcast and halftime show.

The Seattle Seahawks' 29-13 victory over the New England Patriots averaged 124.9 million viewers on NBC, Peacock, Telemundo, NBC Sports Digital and NFL+, according to Nielsen's Big Data + Panel rating system.

That fell short of the 127.7 million U.S. viewers who tuned in for the Philadelphia Eagles' 40-22 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs last year on Fox.

However, Super Bowl XL is the most-watched program in NBC history. The network is celebrating its 100th anniversary this year.

Bad Bunny's halftime show averaged 128.2 million viewers from 8:15 to 8:30 p.m. ET. That would make it the fourth-most-watched halftime behind Kendrick Lamar (133.5 million, 2025), Michael Jackson (133.4 million, 1993) and Usher (129.3 million, 2024).

Peak audience sets U.S. record

The audience for Sunday's game peaked at 137.8 million viewers during the second quarter (7:45-8 p.m. ET), which is a record. That surpassed the previous mark of 137.7 million during the second quarter of last year's Super Bowl.

This year ended a streak of audience increases for the past four Super Bowls. It is the fifth straight year the game has averaged over 100 million viewers.

After three straight years of Super Bowls that came down to the final minute, the past two have lacked excitement.

Sunday's game was the second in Super Bowl history in which a touchdown was not scored in the first three quarters. Seattle was up 12-0 going into the final 15 minutes.

Last year's game was decided in the first half as Philadelphia built a 24-0 lead en route to a 40-22 victory.

Bad Bunny vs. Kid Rock

The Turning Point USA halftime show featuring Kid Rock peaked at 5 million viewers at one point on YouTube.

Nielsen did not measure any of the YouTube livestream viewership. Of the linear networks that carried it, the only one Nielsen measures is broadcast network Charge! Full Nielsen ratings for the prior week will be released Wednesday.

YouTube figures show there have been 21,208,583 views of the alternate halftime show through Tuesday night, according to the conservative organization's page. Bad Bunny's show has had 61,311,972 views on YouTube.

Halftime show on social media

Total social media consumption of Bad Bunny's halftime show set a record of 4 billion views after the first 24 hours, according to the NFL and Ripple Analytics. That is a 137% increase over last year.

The social media figures include fans, owned platforms, broadcast partners and influencers.

The NFL said over 55% of all social views came from international markets.

Full global viewership for the halftime show is expected to be available early next week.

Spanish audience record

Telemundo averaged 3.3 million viewers, making it the most-watched Super Bowl Spanish-language broadcast in the United States. The Super Bowl has been televised in Spanish in the U.S. since 2014.

The audience peaked during the halftime show, averaging 4.8 million viewers -- also making it the most-watched Super Bowl halftime in Spanish-language history.

Olympics benefit from Super Bowl

NBC's "Primetime in Milan" Olympic show, which featured the women's downhill and team figure skating events, averaged 42 million viewers, the network's largest Winter Olympics audience since Day 2 of the 2014 Sochi Games.

It was a 73% increase from the Olympics show after Super Bowl LVI (24.3 million).

"The Super Bowl and the NFL once again delivered a blockbuster audience across the NBC broadcast network, Peacock and Telemundo, and provided an unprecedented lead-in to our 'Primetime in Milan' coverage," NBC Sports president Rick Cordella said in a statement. "The Super Bowl and the Olympics are the two most powerful events in the world, and we salute our talented production, tech and announce teams who delivered best-in-class presentations for our viewers, stations and partners."

Other NFL figures

The NFL playoffs averaged 37 million viewers the first three weekends, up 5% from last year and the second most in the past 10 years.

That followed a regular season that averaged 18.7 million, the second-highest number since audience averages began being kept in 1988. It was a 10% increase from last season.
